name: Ulcerative Colitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ACG/ECCO Guidelines for Diagnosis of Ulcerative Colitis

criteria.description: Endoscopic findings: continuous inflammation starting from rectum, extending proximally without skip lesions; erythema, loss of vascular pattern, friability, erosions, ulcers
Histologic findings: mucosal and submucosal chronic inflammation, crypt abscesses, crypt architectural distortion, goblet cell depletion
Exclusion of infectious colitis (C. difficile, CMV, enteric pathogens)
No small bowel involvement (except backwash ileitis in pancolitis)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation plus endoscopic and histologic findings consistent with UC; exclusion of infectious causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Montreal classification: E1 (ulcerative proctitis), E2 (left-sided/distal), E3 (extensive/pancolitis). Severity: S0 (clinical remission), S1 (mild), S2 (moderate), S3 (severe). Truelove and Witts criteria used for acute severe colitis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Continuous colonic inflammation starting at rectum on endoscopy
pathognomonic.notes: Key distinguishing feature from Crohn's; no skip lesions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Crypt abscesses and architectural distortion on biopsy

rare.notes: Acute colonic dilatation >6 cm with systemic toxicity; surgical emergency
Risk increases with disease extent and duration (>8 years pancolitis)

laboratory: Elevated CRP and ESR (markers of inflammation)
Elevated fecal calprotectin (sensitive marker of colonic inflammation)
ASCA usually negative (helps distinguish from Crohn's)
Stool cultures and C. difficile toxin negative
imaging: Abdominal X-ray: loss of haustral markings (lead pipe colon), colonic dilatation in toxic megacolon
CT abdomen: continuous colonic wall thickening, pericolonic fat stranding, rectal involvement
Colonoscopy with biopsies: erythema, granularity, friability, erosions, pseudopolyps (in chronic disease)
genetic: Overlap with Crohn's disease genetic loci
other: Colonoscopy with step biopsies: continuous mucosal inflammation from rectum, crypt distortion, basal plasmacytosis
Dysplasia surveillance: recommended after 8 years of extensive colitis

distinguishingFeatures: Collagenous or lymphocytic colitis on biopsy

redFlags: >=6 bloody stools/day with systemic toxicity (acute severe colitis - Truelove & Witts criteria)
Colonic dilatation >6 cm on X-ray (toxic megacolon)
Signs of perforation (rebound, guarding, free air)
Failure to respond to IV corticosteroids within 72 hours (rescue therapy or surgery needed)
references: Rubin DT, et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Ulcerative Colitis in Adults. Am J Gastroenterol. 2019;114(3):384-413.
Raine T, et al. ECCO Guidelines on Therapeutics in Ulcerative Colitis: Medical Treatment. J Crohns Colitis. 2022;16(1):2-17.
Ungaro R, et al. Ulcerative colitis. Lancet. 2017;389(10080):1756-1770.
